masterStylePrompt: Use the established hand-drawn 2D historical explainer illustration style. Keep clean dark ink outlines of medium weight, flat muted historical colors, restrained cel-shading and light paper-and-ink texture. Give the dominant subject the clearest silhouette and slightly stronger contrast; simplify secondary detail. Build readable depth through overlap, scale and perspective. Choose staging and visual form for the spoken historical idea: a concrete action, spatial relationship, object detail, reaction or changed state. Stylized historical people belong to the same drawn world as buildings and objects. Depict historically specific individuals with believable adult structure, small calmly drawn eyes, economical facial lines and purposeful body contact with their surroundings. Show emotion through the situation, gaze and posture; use large expressions only when the narrated action calls for them. Keep recurring identities stable without cloning unrelated faces or exaggerating their features merely to make them different. A group has a clear primary action; secondary people respond in ways appropriate to their roles. Keep architecture, clothing and equipment historically grounded. Render no text by default; only the exact approved cover or editorial words may appear when explicitly requested. Do not drift toward photorealism, a glossy animation-film look or caricature.
sceneStyleAnchor: Keep the established channel illustration: clean dark ink contours, muted flat colors, subtle cel-shadows and light paper texture, with one clear subject and a quieter background. When people appear, depict individualized stylized historical humans with believable proportions, small unexaggerated eyes, sparing facial lines and scene-specific purposeful poses. Preserve the individual appearance of recurring people. Keep figures and surroundings in the same drawing style.

characterGeometry.headToBodyRatio: For a complete standing adult, approximately 1:7 overall anatomical height (roughly 1:6.5 to 1:7.5); account for age and pose. Never derive this ratio from a cropped visible body.
characterGeometry.head: Simple human head mass connected plausibly to the neck, with a readable jaw and no oversized spherical head.
characterGeometry.face: Small eyes inside lightly drawn lids, restrained brows, a simple nose indication and economical mouth lines. A relaxed or closed mouth is the normal resting state; larger expressions follow a concrete narrated action. Use a few flat shadow shapes instead of etched wrinkles or portrait rendering.
characterGeometry.body: Believable adult structure within simplified 2D drawing: neck, shoulders, ribcage and pelvis align with the action. Standing weight reaches the feet and floor; sitting, leaning or floating follows the actual scene. Avoid identical symmetrical mannequin poses.
characterGeometry.handsFeet: Describe which hand holds, supports, rests on or reaches toward which object. Prominent hands have coherent fingers and wrists; simplify small hands without inventing extra parts. Keep feet in believable contact with their support unless the action explicitly removes it.
characterGeometry.variationSource: age impression, face shape, hair, beard, headwear, height, build, clothing silhouette, armor, accessories, props, posture and expression
characterGeometry.cloneRule: Unrelated people must not reuse the same face, hair, clothing silhouette and body proportions. Recurring characters intentionally keep identifying traits. Avoid three officers with the same age, moustache, frown and head shape.

controlledVariationPolicy.goal: same illustrator and rendering DNA, different scene direction, strong visual rhythm and individualized historical people
antiRepetition: Do not reuse the same composition merely for consistency.
Do not default every character scene to the same medium-wide frontal view.
Do not default every architecture scene to the same centered wide view.
Do not populate unrelated scenes with the same generic face, hair, tunic and body silhouette.
Do not create three similar static character interactions in sequence.
Do not create three abstract explanation-only scenes in sequence.
Change visual form, shot scale, viewpoint or framing when narrative understanding benefits from it.
Reuse nearly the same angle only for deliberate before-after or state-change continuity.

globalNegativePrompt: Preserve the same drawn illustration family across the sequence. No photorealism, 3D, glossy animation-film rendering, anime, painterly realism, graphic-novel realism, chibi proportions, neon colors or generic identical stickman clones. Do not give every person wide white-ringed eyes, heavy arched brows, an open shouting mouth or raised gesturing hands. Avoid invented facial wrinkles, mannequin symmetry, inconsistent figure/environment rendering, oversized heads, contorted joints, extra fingers, impossible grips and unsupported objects. Never draw BILD, IMAGE, SCENE, image numbers, watermarks or pseudo-writing. Non-cover art remains text-free unless an explicit legacy EDITORIAL_TEXT instruction supplies the exact permitted words.

characterQualityPolicy.acceptanceRule: Reject/regenerate in Phase 2 any prominent human that appears silly, overly cartoonish, anatomy-inconsistent, face-cloned or interacts implausibly with objects. Never change locked images in Phase 3.
characterQualityPolicy.faceDetail: Small readable features and a few flat shade shapes; avoid heavily etched or over-modelled faces.
characterQualityPolicy.groupActing: One primary action with relevant secondary attention; do not stage everyone as simultaneously pointing, shouting or panicking.

refinementScope: Refine the existing drawn figures only; preserve channel palette, linework, shading, environments and historical illustration identity. Authorised by the user on 21 October 2026. Not visually approved until tested with user-generated images.
figureDrawingPrompt: Draw adult figures with balanced heads, necks, shoulders and limbs; use about seven head lengths for a complete standing body, never the height of a cropped figure. Eyes are small within lightly drawn lids, with restrained brows and sparing mouth lines. Keep facial shading to a few flat shapes. Convey the planned emotion through gaze, posture and the specific task. Make weight, hand contact, grips and object support physically coherent. In a group, give one action visual priority; others respond with their own relevant attention. Keep hair, face shape, build and period clothing individual without enlarging features for contrast.
backgroundFigurePrompt: Draw distant people as a few coherent body and clothing shapes with readable activity and stance. Reduce facial detail with distance; do not add tiny theatrical expressions or floating hands. Use the same ink and flat-color style as the foreground.
legacySceneStyleAnchors: Keep the locked channel drawing DNA unchanged: flat hand-drawn 2D history-explainer illustration, clean dark ink outlines, muted flat historical colors, subtle cel shading and light paper-and-ink texture. When people appear, depict individualized stylized historical humans with readable simplified anatomy and distinct silhouettes, faces, hair, clothing and posture; never default to identical generic stickman clones. Give the frame one clear visual idea and avoid a static generic medium talking-head composition. Do not copy the previous scene's composition unless continuity specifically requires it. Draw people with restrained natural expressions, balanced adult proportions, coherent hands and believable gestures; no overacted comic faces or repeated generic officer portraits.
